title: X Feed Digest
summary: Developer AI tools spent the batch smoothing real workflow pain: Codex added richer app-window context, Antigravity rushed IDE fixes plus another quota reset, and even small UX tweaks were framed around keeping heavy users productive.

The clearest financial/regulatory signal was a sharper China clamp on offshore broker access, with feed commentary centering on Futu, Tiger, and Longbridge as channels mainland investors used to reach U.S. and Hong Kong markets.

Specialized AI products kept getting more practical rather than more theatrical, especially in clinical and research workflows where voice interaction and paper-centric organization are starting to feel mature.

summary.html: Watch: Security and policy risk stayed elevated, from renewed SonicWall reconnaissance to immigration-policy criticism framed as a direct hit to U.S. AI competitiveness.

items.title: @OpenAIDevs: Codex Appshots
items.body: OpenAI shipped Appshots for Codex, letting a Mac user attach a live app window so the agent sees both text and a screenshot. That narrows the gap between code-only agents and debugging real UI state.

items.title: @_mohansolo: Antigravity IDE Reset
items.body: After backlash around the IDE experience, Antigravity clarified that developer IDE support is staying, pushed connection/setup fixes, and reset everyone's Gemini quota again. The signal is that throughput and workflow friction are now product-critical, not secondary polish.

items.title: @EvidenceOpen: Voice Mode for Physicians
items.body: OpenEvidence launched voice mode across web and mobile so physicians can ask, listen, and interrupt naturally while moving through rounds or calls. It feels meaningful because the product is adapting to messy clinical workflows instead of expecting doctors to sit and type at a desk.

items.title: @scite: Research Collections
items.body: Scite added Collections, a workspace for curating papers, getting Smart Citation alerts, and asking targeted questions against a specific bundle of literature. It's a small but genuinely useful research workflow upgrade if you live in papers all day.

items.title: @qingyue820: Offshore Broker Crackdown
items.body: Feed commentary converged on Beijing's move against Futu, Tiger, and Longbridge, with this post arguing regulators are confiscating mainland-derived revenue and tightening a popular route into U.S. and Hong Kong equities. The actionable takeaway is that mainland access to offshore broker rails looks materially riskier now.

items.title: @HedgieMarkets: The AI Subsidy Era Ends
items.body: One of the sharper market takes in the batch argued that usage-based billing, price hikes, and enterprise budget blowups are colliding across AI software. Even if some sourcing is secondhand, the framing is useful for anyone underwriting AI SaaS margins or internal AI budgets.

items.title: @S3Partners: Wendy's Short Squeeze Setup
items.body: S3 flagged Wendy's as a live event-driven setup: short interest is up 94% YTD while Trian explores financing a take-private deal. If financing firms up, bears could be forced to cover into a tight tape.

items.title: @GreyNoiseIO: SonicWall Recon Warning
items.body: GreyNoise is seeing SonicWall scanning activity that resembles the pattern ahead of February's CVE-2026-0400 wave, with May 12 marking the largest daily session volume in 90 days. If you run SonicWall gear, this is the clearest patch-and-hunt warning in the batch.

items.title: @AndrewYNg: Immigration as AI Policy
items.body: Andrew Ng argued that forcing green-card applicants to apply from outside the U.S. is not just cruel but strategically self-defeating for science and AI talent. The useful signal is that immigration policy is again being framed as part of national AI competitiveness, not a separate debate.

items.title: @CARMA_411: Adaptive AI Governance
items.body: CARMA released a governance paper that moves past vague principles and names concrete failure modes plus structural requirements for adaptive AI oversight. It is useful if you want a systems-style frame for governance rather than the usual slogan thread.
